text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Truckers Association of Zambia said on Sunday it feared that the crop marketing exercise would be derailed because of a fuel shortage in the country. Association chairman Charles Madondo said most truckers had parked their engines because of the shortage, caused by maintenance problems at port Dar-es-Salaam.

- The opposition Zambia Democratic Congress insisted that there would be a power vacuum in Zambia after October 31, when the government's five-year mandate runs out unless elections are held before then. Party president Dean Mungomba was reacting to the announcement that presidential and parliamentary elections would be held on November 18.
- A civic group said it fears that elections set for November 18 may be disrupted unless president Frederick Chiluba calls for inter-party talks to resolved electoral differences.

- The Legal Resource foundation has said the government's continued stay in office after the disolution of Parliament on October 18 is unconstitutional and has urged political stakeholders to challenge it in the courts of law.
